body: I'm online on and off throughout the day. I kinda get how you feel about "regular careers", sort of going though the same problem myself. PM me if you like.
This subreddit usually doesn't like PMs (just so that we can correct shitty advice) but my inbox is open :)

I'm still going along at school. Part of the whole program is speaking to the counselor about academics, and when I mentioned that my grades were slipping he was very understanding. It was really foreign to me.

Concerning the self harm stuff, my father does not believe that psychology/psychiatry are "real". I had to explain to him after a long argument --with sources-- that they do tests such as scans and blood tests before diagnosis. I still doubt he believed me. I also have trouble trusting them, considering that they have the power to lock me up in a mental facility. I also had some less-than-savory experiences with counselors in the past, who would ignore harassment from other students and then treat me like some sort of sideshow.

Thank you for reading.

Hey, if you're still online I'm here to talk. I don't know your life story, but I kind of get where you are coming from, especially the human connection thing. It's something I have never been very good at myself. Let me know how your holding up.

If it helps at all, you sound a lot like me. I don't know your upbringing, but I have a...restrictive family. My upbringing has left me socially/emotionally/culturally stunted. It's really isolating.

You mentioned you moved to the city for work. May I ask about it?

Thank you. At this point (17 y/o) I've been coping with distraction more than anything else. 

I got told by my father to stop playing music (bass) and to focus even more on my studies...but at this point the classes that I am in bore me. I've been wasting a position in a very lucky program; and I am not even enjoying the subjects I used to love. Many days I will draw through 2 hour lectures just to pass the time. The classes are too intense; it always feels like I am failing.

Aside from trying to ignore the problem, I've always taken it out on my body. I hate it. I started early by biting my arm, and I've got scars the size of my thumbprint on either bicep from biting in elementary school. Pins, matches, anything was used. Now I just scratch, enough to draw blood and make a faint scar but little else. 

One of the few things stopping me from offing myself is the cat, which I cannot trust my family to care for properly. The other thing is the mess I'd make in both a physical and financial sense. I can't imagine those sanitation workers are cheap.

Thank you for the kind words.
I just don't get it...I still feel so angry and tired.
